text:
Ellen: Heads up — Cobalt bank POC kickoff tomorrow. They want written acceptance criteria for PrivateDeploy connectivity and a short firewall/egress checklist. Can someone draft? cc @Sam @Ravi
Sam: I can own the checklist. Quick clarifying Q: Cobalt confirmed they want the connector in their VPC + traffic egress through their on‑prem proxy, correct?
Ravi: Correct. Architecture is: customer VPC with Redwood connector in private subnet, interface endpoint (PrivateLink) back to Redwood control plane, and all model egress proxied to their onprem TLS SNI proxy. Must preserve client IP for their logging.
Priya: FYI security will ask about key handling (KMS/HSM), audit logs retention, and whether we use mutual TLS to the proxy. They also want an operator-run kill switch for egress in case of incident.
Sam: Proposal: two supported topologies for the doc — 1) PrivateLink + customer proxy (recommended for least blast radius), 2) TGW/VPC peering + NAT egress (fallback if PrivateLink not allowed). List pros/cons and required firewall rules.
Ravi: Minimal firewall snippet we should give them (outbound from connector hosts):
```
# allow outbound TLS to Redwood control plane and model pools
ALLOW tcp 443 to *.redwood-hosted.net (or specific FQDNs we provide)
# allow DNS
ALLOW udp 53 to customer DNS resolver or 8.8.8.8
# allow NTP
ALLOW udp 123 to NTP pool
# if using management plane over PrivateLink: allow interface endpoint IPs (we'll supply)
```
Sam: Also call out these requirements: preserve source IP (no NAT before their proxy), stable egress IPs (customer will need static allowlist), and SNI passthrough for TLS-inspect setups.
Priya: For the security questionnaire: include articulations for data-in-transit (TLS 1.2+), key storage (customer KMS integration or Redwood-managed with attestation), and audit logging (30/90/365d options).
deploy-bot: Reminder: run the connectivity smoke test after whitelisting: 
```
curl -v https://<connector-internal-ip>/healthz --resolve "api.redwood-hosted.net:443:<connector-internal-ip>"
```
Ravi: Quick checklist I’ll add to the doc:
- confirm interface endpoint creation & SG rules
- validate route table to subnet
- whitelist FQDNs/IPs and test TLS handshake
- verify client IP preservation (tcpdump sample)
- run curl health check from a bastion host
Sam: Pricing/contract note for Ellen: PrivateDeploy quote = base platform license + monthly infra fee. If they require static egress IPs and dedicated capacity we upsell reserved capacity (add-on). I’ll paste exact numbers in the proposal doc.
Ellen: Perfect. Can you guys keep it to one page checklist + 1 page ops runbook? I want to send to Cobalt SSO by EOD.
Priya: Will do. I’ll add answers for the security questionnaire (short bullets) and the attestation options.
Ravi: I’ll attach tcpdump and sample iptables commands in the runbook.
Ellen: Thanks all — I’ll compile and send. :thumbsup:
